name: Ketorolac
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.indication: Moderately severe acute pain, under 65 years
usual_adult_dose.dose: IV 30 mg or IM 60 mg single dose; or 30 mg IV/IM every 6 hours, maximum 120 mg/day

usual_adult_dose.indication: 65 years or older, renally impaired, or under 50 kg
usual_adult_dose.dose: IV 15 mg or IM 30 mg single dose; or 15 mg every 6 hours, maximum 60 mg/day
Maximum 5 days combined injection and oral

key_interactions.effect: Less blood-pressure and diuretic effect; risk of acute kidney injury and hyperkalemia, especially in older, volume-depleted or CKD patients (label).
key_interactions.action: Avoid the triple combination where possible; if used, check creatinine and potassium within 1 to 2 weeks and keep the patient hydrated.
Avoid if possible; otherwise monitor for bleeding.

key_interactions.effect: More gastrointestinal toxicity without added benefit (label).

key_interactions.action: Monitor drug levels and kidney function.

common: Abdominal pain, dyspepsia, nausea, gastrointestinal pain
serious: Acute kidney injury, papillary necrosis, hyperkalemia

contraindications: Advanced renal impairment or risk of renal failure from volume depletion
Active or past peptic ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding
Suspected or confirmed cerebrovascular bleeding, hemorrhagic diathesis, high bleeding risk
Prophylactic analgesic before major surgery; CABG setting
Concurrent aspirin or other NSAIDs, probenecid or pentoxifylline
Asthma or allergic reaction after aspirin or NSAIDs
monitoring: Volume status, creatinine, urine output, potassium

pk.half_life_eskd: 6 to 19 hours in renal impairment (single dose; label)
